newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Major index volatilities hold up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Major index volatilities hold up.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. stock index futures held firm Tuesday even as the market's choppy tone of late eased, traders said.
In early afternoon trading, the S&P 100 index was up a fraction at 823.60 after having traded between 818.32 and 824.43, a record intraday high.
The S&P 500 index was off 0.35 at 837.71. It traded between 832.97 and 838.49.
June S&P 500 futures lost 1.30 to 840.05, putting them near the top of their 836.10 to 842.50 intraday range.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's (CBOE) volatility index, which is priced off certain OEX options, was up 0.51, or about 2.3 percent, at 22.47.
Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX at the CBOE, said volatility in the OEX firmed as call buying emerged when the market recovered early losses.
In morning trading, put buying was fairly heavy and put spreads were popular, he added.
"Volatility is holding firm," said one S&P 500 futures options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
"I think people are waiting on any action from the bonds," the trader said. "The futures market has been pretty cautiously range-trading."
After last week's heavy activity, he said, futures options players were taking a breather to gear up for the expiration of May options at the end of the week.
"As far as the expiration, they'll start unwinding (May positions) tomorrow and Thursday and really roll their sleeves up and get down to business," he said.
He said, however, that June options were becoming more active.
In the OEX, Callahan noted, overall turnover was led by the May 820 call, which traded 10,255 contracts.
"There might be some rolling of positions, but we haven't seen any significant rolls," he said. "There's been more activity in June, both puts and calls," compared to the last few sessions.
He added that given this week's expiration and some key economic data including April producer and consumer price reports, volatilities would likely remain firm.

In the OEX June series, the heaviest action was in the 770 call and put, which traded 1,635 and 1,380 contracts, respectively, and the 810 put and call, which traded 1,175 and 1,000 contracts, respectively.
Other busy May OEX options included the 810, 825 and 830 calls and the 810, 815 and 820 puts.
